steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Ops left `/app/bin/gasketd` on this image. `bind` reads every card under `/app/buscards` and refreshes `/app/mistwell/roster.json`. `jab` takes one integer and prints `{"wire":N,"reply":S}`. `cork` writes `/app/corkbay/seal.json` with `served` (LABEL values in card order) and `status`. Source fixes under `/app` are required. Modules live in directories listed by `/app/opscribe/MAP.txt`. Static copies of the roster or seal objects are not enough. After that work `/app/bin/gasketd` must start with `\x7fELF`. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/gasketd bind`, `/app/bin/gasketd jab`, and `/app/bin/gasketd cork`.

A newly added card still lets `bind` and `cork` finish, yet `jab` of its WIRE prints `fallthrough` instead of that card's REPLY. Every card must answer `jab` with its own REPLY. An integer that no card lists must print `fallthrough`. `cork` must exit non-zero when the running hopper cannot serve every card, and `status` must not be `sealed` in that case. Each card has a `LABEL` line, a `WIRE` line (integer), and a `REPLY` line.


Current terminal state:
Current Terminal Screen:
root@3d8fef45a128:/app#

Analysis: We are at a root shell in /app with no prior inspection shown. We need identify the source/module layout, inspect the card data and current gasketd behavior, then patch source, rebuild the ELF binary, and test bind/jab/cork including failure semantics.
Plan: Inspect MAP.txt, the /app tree, the current binary type, all card contents, and any build/source files. Also run the existing commands to establish their current behavior.

' '--- MAP ---'; cat /app/opscribe/MAP.txt; printf '%s
' '--- FILES ---'; find /app -maxdepth 4 -type f -printf '%p
' | sort; printf '%s

printf '%s\n' '--- BUILD FILES ---'; find /app -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -name 'Makefile' -o -name '*.c' -o -name '*.h' -o -name '*.cc' -o -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.rs' -o -name '*.go' -o -name '*.py' -o -name '*.sh' \) -print -exec sh -c 'echo "### $1"; sed -n "1,240p" "$1"' sh {} \;

echo '--- CURRENT BEHAVIOR ---'; /app/bin/gasketd bind; echo "bind_rc=$?"; cat /app/mistwell/roster.json 2>/dev/null; for f in /app/buscards/*; do w=$(sed -n 's/^WIRE[[:space:]]*[=:][[:space:]]*//p;s/^WIRE[[:space:]]\+//p' "$f" | head -1); [ -n "$w" ] && { echo "jab $w"; /app/bin/gasketd jab "$w"; echo "rc=$?"; }; done; /app/bin/gasketd cork; echo "cork_rc=$?"; cat /app/corkbay/seal.json 2>/dev/null

steps.message:
Analysis: The defect is in the compiled hopper: it embeds emit.lst at build time, stores rows by their ordinal position rather than WIRE, and truncates processing through a hard-coded span of 8. Thus bind sees all nine cards while jab does not. Cork only checks whether refreshed roster text contains labels, so it can report sealed without confirming that the running hopper can answer those cards. The hopper must load live cards at command execution, key entries by WIRE, and cork must compare every card against the actual hopper mapping. Using a signed integer key also lets an unlisted integer, including one outside u8 range, cleanly fall through.
Plan: Rewrite hopmat/table.rs to construct a live WIRE-keyed map from slipread cards and expose a per-card service check. Change card WIRE storage and jab parsing to i64. Rewrite cork validation to require the live hopper's slot at each card's WIRE to match both that card's LABEL and REPLY; duplicate conflicting WIREs will therefore leave the seal open and return non-zero. Rebuild with stoke.sh, verify ELF magic, test all cards and unknown integers, then temporarily add a conflicting card to prove cork failure before restoring normal generated outputs.

arguments.keystrokes: echo '--- ELF MAGIC ---'; od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/gasketd; echo '--- NORMAL TEST ---'; /app/bin/gasketd bind; echo "bind_rc=$?"; cat /app/mistwell/roster.json; for f in /app/buscards/*.card; do w=$(awk '$1=="WIRE"{print $2}' "$f"); expected=$(awk '$1=="REPLY"{$1=""; sub(/^ /,""); print}' "$f"); got=$(/app/bin/gasketd jab "$w"); printf 'wire=%s expected=%s got=%s\n' "$w" "$expected" "$got"; done; /app/bin/gasketd jab 999; /app/bin/gasketd jab -5; /app/bin/gasketd cork; echo "cork_rc=$?"; cat /app/corkbay/seal.json

echo '--- FAILURE TEST ---'; cat > /app/buscards/z_conflict.card <<'EOF'
LABEL CONFLICT_TEST
WIRE 1
REPLY conflict-reply
EOF
/app/bin/gasketd bind; /app/bin/gasketd cork; rc=$?; echo "conflict_cork_rc=$rc"; cat /app/corkbay/seal.json; rm -f /app/buscards/z_conflict.card; /app/bin/gasketd bind; /app/bin/gasketd cork; echo "restored_cork_rc=$?"; cat /app/corkbay/seal.json; test "$rc" -ne 0; test "$(od -An -tx1 -N4 /app/bin/gasketd | tr -d ' \n')" = 7f454c46

steps.message:
Analysis: The source has been fixed and rebuilt successfully. The hopper now loads the live card set, indexes entries by each card's WIRE, supports integer wires beyond u8, returns each card's own REPLY, and returns fallthrough for unlisted integers. Cork validates every card against the running hopper and exits 1 with open status when duplicate/conflicting wires prevent all cards from being served. Normal cork output preserves card order. The rebuilt /app/bin/gasketd has ELF magic 7f 45 4c 46. Temporary test data was removed and normal roster/seal outputs were restored.
Plan: No further work is required. All specified behavior, dynamic-card handling, failure behavior, source persistence, and ELF binary requirements have been verified.
